steps.title: Orient — take the platform tour
steps.description: Skim the "Using this app" tab below: what each module does and how they fit together.
steps.teaches: Before touching data, know the map: ingest → store → transform → serve.

steps.title: Register a connector
steps.description: Create a connector on the Connectors page — a named, reusable source (sample, CSV/JSON upload or REST URL).
steps.teaches: Connectors decouple WHERE data comes from from HOW it is ingested.

steps.title: Run an ingestion
steps.description: Pull data through a connector (or upload a file) until an ingestion reports success.
steps.teaches: Ingestion is a job with observable status — not a side effect of uploading.

steps.title: Explore a versioned dataset
steps.description: Open a dataset in the studio: preview rows, check the inferred schema, look at its version history.
steps.teaches: Datasets are immutable: every write produces a NEW version, never an overwrite.

steps.title: Write a code transform
steps.description: Create a workbook (SQL, JavaScript or Python) in Transforms that reads a dataset and outputs another.
steps.teaches: Code transforms are versioned first-class assets, like in a real code repo.

steps.title: Run the transform
steps.description: Execute the workbook and confirm it wrote a new dataset version from its output.
steps.teaches: Running code produces immutable outputs — same contract as visual pipelines.

steps.title: Build a pipeline graph
steps.description: Save a pipeline version in the visual builder (source → filter/derive → output).
steps.teaches: Pipelines are declarative DAGs; saving a version snapshots the whole graph.

steps.title: Run a pipeline to success
steps.description: Trigger a run and watch it go green on the Orchestration jobs table.
steps.teaches: A run records what it read and wrote — provenance is captured, not reconstructed.

steps.title: Schedule a pipeline
steps.description: Add a schedule (an interval) to a pipeline so the Bun scheduler service picks it up.
steps.teaches: Orchestration is outside the app: a separate service calls credentialed endpoints.

steps.title: Register an object type
steps.description: Back an object type with a dataset in Ontology and pick its primary key.
steps.teaches: The ontology projects rows into business objects people can reason about.

steps.title: Execute an action (write-back)
steps.description: Submit an action on an object and see the new dataset version it produced.
steps.teaches: Actions are governed writes: UI → action → new immutable version → pipelines react.

steps.title: Build a dashboard
steps.description: Add at least one widget backed by a dataset on the Dashboards page.
steps.teaches: Dashboards read the consumer pointer — the same view decisions see.

steps.title: Mark a sensitive column
steps.description: Attach a marking with a minRole to a dataset column and view it as a lower role.
steps.teaches: Governance is enforced at READ time: masking happens per viewer, per cell.

steps.title: Publish through the quality gate
steps.description: Turn on a dataset's publication gate, ingest a draft, then publish it (see the dataset banner).
steps.teaches: Preview → validate → approve → publish: bad data never reaches consumers.

steps.title: Replay a run from its manifest
steps.description: Open any run's build record on Orchestration and click "Replay from recorded inputs".
steps.teaches: Reproducible builds: retry uses latest inputs; replay uses the RECORDED ones.

steps.title: Trace version-level lineage
steps.description: Open the lineage impact panel and follow which input versions fed an output version.
steps.teaches: Dataset-level edges say WHAT connects; version-level edges say WHEN and WITH WHAT.

steps.title: Mint an API token
steps.description: Create a token on API Tokens and call the public API with it (see the curl snippet).
steps.teaches: Machine access is credentialed, rate-limited and logged per request.

steps.title: Read the DE concepts
steps.description: Work through the "DE concepts" tab and connect each idea to the module you just used.
steps.teaches: The tooling changes; the concepts (immutability, lineage, gates) transfer.
